The task requires no deep Minecraft domain knowledge beyond knowing how to break a block, and its completion is easily verified by checking inventory for the resulting items or by confirming the block no longer exists at its placed position. milestones.description: Uses inventory_has for flower_pot because breaking a potted_poppy block drops a flower_pot and a poppy as separate items — the block name 'potted_poppy' never appears as an inventory item. The player starts with no flower_pot in inventory, and there is no other source of flower_pot in this scene, so having one uniquely proves the potted poppy was mined. Preferred over count_in_box_at_most (block removal check) because inventory_has is coordinate-independent and more robust for mine tasks.

scene_description: A simple stone pedestal with a potted poppy placed 3 blocks from spawn in a forested area. The stone cross-shaped platform (5 stone blocks at ground level) elevates the potted poppy to eye level, making it easy to spot and mine. The player spawns facing roughly toward the potted poppy and can walk directly to it.
task_text: Find and mine the potted poppy sitting on the stone pedestal nearby.
design_notes: The potted poppy is placed at relative coordinates (~3, ~1, ~3) on top of a stone block. Four additional stone blocks form a cross-shaped platform at ground level (~0) for visual contrast against the natural terrain. The potted poppy is at Y+1 (one block above ground), making it roughly chest/eye level and easy to target. Breaking a potted_poppy block drops both a flower_pot and a poppy item separately. No tools or inventory items are required — potted plants break instantly with bare hands.
